title: Aunt Carrie, first drums and the second line bands
summary: His Aunt Carrie, a teacher and pianist, and his mother encouraged him; she bought his first drums. He beat on chairs, followed New Orleans second-line bands and moved there at about ten.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Getting my first drums, with or without lessons

blocks.x: think.
Well, now your parents, were they musicians in any way?
Well my Aunt Carrie.
She more or less brought you up didn't she?
Yes, she's the one that partly raised me in a way because she was an old school teacher and I used to go to Bunkie and (Upper Lousay?) and Mamou (Marmout?), that's in Louisiana.
Let's see what we've got now. Now your Aunt, she played the piano?
Yes she did.
Did she encourage you in music?
Well she sure did because my mother did also you know. Because my aunt bought me my first set of drums. Yes.
When did you first sort of begin to feel that you wanted to play the drums?
Oh, from way back. I was a real small boy.
What, you used to beat on chairs and things?
Yes. I used to beat on chairs
and things like that. And used to get the chair rounds out of the kitchen chairs and make sticks and play, you know. Beat them out.
And I suppose seeing bands marching in the streets, did that have something to do with it?
Oh yes indeed. Sure, I used to love to follow those bands you know. They called it the second line you know.
What sort of bands would they have in Bunkie, sort of marching bands?
No, not in Bunkie. This was in New Orleans. Yes, yes.
Well when did you go there?
Oh, when I was about ten years old.
Oh, ten.
Went there to live, to stay, yes.
